subject: Request: Full penetration testing report and remediation status (Hartwell Health)
messages:
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@hartwellhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Cho <emily.cho@hartwellhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for penetration test report and scope clarification - urgent

Soojin —

We're seeing some anomalous API calls in our logs that touch token-scrubbing endpoints. Given the sensitivity of PHI being proxied by our integration, Hartwell's security team is requesting the latest penetration testing report for Redwood's hosted inference surface and clarification on the test scope (external vs internal, authenticated pathways covered, third-party components included).

Specifically we need:
- The most recent pentest summary and full report (redactions acceptable for vendor tooling IP)
- A clear scope statement indicating which endpoints and authentication flows were in-scope
- A remediation status for any findings that touch token handling, auth, or data exfiltration vectors

This is an urgent ask from our CISO (I'm on the thread). Please advise whether you can share a redacted full report or a compliance package that covers the above. If you have a timeline for delivery, include it.

Thanks,
Rajiv Patel
CISO, Hartwell Health
security@hartwellhealth.com

[attachment: evidence_request_form_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report and scope clarification - urgent

Rajiv — thank you for raising this and sorry for the alarm. Looping in our security and legal folks to scope this properly; they'll confirm what we can share and what needs redaction.

Immediate notes:
- We have a 2025 third-party penetration assessment of our hosted API surface; vendor contract requires redaction of selective infra-specific exploit PoCs. We can provide a redacted report + a technical findings summary that addresses auth/token concerns.
- Mina will confirm whether authenticated pathways (customer-specific tokens, token exchange endpoints) were explicitly tested or covered under the 'authenticated flows' portion of the scope.
- If you prefer, we can provide a short runbook of mitigations and timelines for any open items and schedule a 30-min call with our security engineering team.

Mina / Vivek / Laura — can you advise availability to produce a redacted package and estimated delivery for Hartwell?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@hartwellhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report and scope clarification - Redwood response

Rajiv / Team —

Thanks for the flag. I want to be transparent about what we can share and how we'll handle the request:

1) Report availability
- We ran an independent penetration assessment in Nov 2025 covering the hosted API public surface, the ingestion/processing pipeline, and the token exchange service. The original full report contains vendor PoCs and low-level infra steps that are covered by a non-disclosure clause with our testing partner.
- We can produce a redacted PDF of the full report that removes vendor PoCs and any infra-specific exploit code. That redacted report will retain all findings, severity ratings, and remediation recommendations.

2) Scope clarification
- In-scope: public API endpoints (text/generate, chat), token exchange endpoints used by redirect flows, rate-limiting bypass checks, and the hosted runtime's plugin/tooling interface.
- Out-of-scope: customer-managed on-prem/private deployments and our internal CI/CD environment.

3) Auth/token-specific findings and remediation status
- Finding A (medium): transient token exposure in debug logs - remediated by Nov 2025; mitigation: log redaction + rotating key policy; verified in November retest.
- Finding B (high): insufficient validation of third-party callback URLs in a legacy webhook handler - patched in Dec 2025; monitors added; remediation in PROD; follow-up scans show no regression.
- No findings classified as data exfiltration vectors were confirmed.

4) Deliverables and timeline
- Today: Provide a high-level Findings Summary via email (this thread) and share SOC 2 control mapping for the affected areas (attached).
- 48 hours: Deliver a redacted PDF report (vendor PoCs removed) + a remediation tracker (CSV) with dates and verification evidence.
- If Hartwell requires the unredacted report under a mutual NDA, we can arrange a controlled sharing process through our legal team; otherwise redacted report should satisfy compliance reviews.

I'll attach the initial summary and the SOC 2 control mapping now. If you have specific log entries / API ids you can paste here I can correlate immediately.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

[attachment: socs2_control_mapping_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Mina — thank you, that is helpful. Two follow-ups:

1) We will accept a redacted report to start. Please confirm which fields you will redact so our audit team can sign off without an NDA first (i.e., do you redact PoCs + IP only, or also exploitable configuration data?)

2) I'll paste two sample request-ids that correspond to the anomalous entries. If you can correlate them back to token handling or any of the patched endpoints, that will help us close the loop quickly.

Request IDs: 9f7a2c-20260304-03, 9f7a2c-20260304-07

We'd also like a short call with your security engineers tomorrow morning PST to walk through the remediation evidence. Can Mina / Vivek confirm availability?

-Rajiv

Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report and scope clarification - Redacted report & remediation tracker

Rajiv / Team —

Attached are the deliverables we promised: a redacted penetration test report and a remediation tracker (INC-4521) that maps each finding to the shipped fix, test date, and verification evidence. See attachments: redwood_pen_test_redacted_2025-11.pdf, remediation_tracker_INC-4521.csv, socs2_control_mapping_v2.xlsx.

To answer your earlier question on redaction policy: we redact vendor PoCs and any exploit code or low-level infra commands. We do not redact finding titles, severity, affected components (e.g., token-exchange service), remediation notes, or verification evidence. We will not redact configuration-level settings that would materially enable replication of an exploit.

Summary of token/auth-related items (extracted from the report):
- Finding A (medium) - transient token exposure in pre-prod debug logs; remediation: log sanitization + forced rotation (verified 2025-11-20). Evidence: log scrub job output sample (hash redacted).
- Finding C (low) - insufficient token TTL enforcement on legacy session tokens; remediation: TTL reduced and enforcement in early 2026; added monitoring alert (verified 2026-01-10).

We were able to correlate your request-ids: 9f7a2c-20260304-03 and -07. Both correspond to a noisy healthcheck routine that hit a misconfigured webhook proxy during a maintenance window; no token exfiltration vectors were observed. I've included the correlation notes in the remediation tracker.

If you want the unredacted report under NDA, Laura can start the NDA process and produce a secure transfer link. Otherwise, please confirm receipt and whether the redacted package satisfies Hartwell's audit needs. We're available for the call tomorrow 09:00-11:00 PST; Vivek and I can join.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
mina.haddad@redwood.com
